pathogen_scientific_name.value: Rice tungro bacilliform virus (RTBV) and Rice tungro spherical virus (RTSV)
pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Rice tungro bacilliform virus ( RTBV ) bacilliform capsid, circular ds DNA genome and Rice tungro spherical virus (RTSV) isometric capsid ss RNA genome.

type_of_disease.quote: Rice tungro disease is caused by the combination of two viruses, which are transmitted by leafhoppers.

affected_parts.quote: Plants are markedly stunted. Leaves show yellow to orange discoloration and interveinal chlorosis . Young leaves are sometimes mottled while rusty spots appear on older leaves. Tillering is reduced with poor root system.

summary.value: Tungro causes yellow or orange-yellow leaf discoloration beginning at the leaf tip and extending downward, along with stunting, reduced tillers, delayed flowering, and small, incompletely exserted panicles with sterile or partially filled grains covered with dark brown blotches.
summary.quote: It causes leaf discoloration, stunted growth, reduced tiller numbers and sterile or partly filled grains.

diagnostic_features.value: Yellow or orange-yellow discoloration that begins from the leaf tip and extends down to the blade or lower leaf portion; infected leaves may also show mottled or striped appearance, rust-colored spots, and inter-veinal necrosis, accompanied by stunting and partially filled grains covered with dark brown blotches; young leaves are sometimes mottled while rusty spots appear on older leaves, and panicles are small with few, deformed and chaffy grains.
diagnostic_features.quote: Yellow or orange-yellow discoloration is noticeable in tungro-infected plants. Discoloration begins from the leaf tip and extends down to the blade or the lower leaf portion. Infected leaves may also show mottled or striped appearance, rust-colored spots, and inter-veinal necrosis.

look_alikes.quote: the yellowing of the plant and its stunted height can be confused as nitrogen and zinc deficiencies and water stress, pest infestation such as stem borer infestation, plant hopper infestation, and rat damage, and other diseases such as grassy stunt virus disease and orange leaf.

conflicts.note: IRRI Knowledge Bank lists Seed as an affected part (sterile/partly filled grains) rather than Root; eagri.org lecture notes mention poor root system explicitly.
Journal article only mentions yellowing and stunting without specifying root or seed involvement.

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: The disease is caused by a fungus named Rhizoctonia solani.

type_of_disease.quote: The disease is caused by a fungus named Rhizoctonia solani.

affected_parts.quote: Advanced leaf sheath and stem infection: the sheath has been girdled and the leaf is dead.

summary.value: Initial symptoms are oblong, water-soaked lesions on leaf sheaths at or near the water line, which develop a grayish-white center with a dark purplish- or reddish-brown margin; lesions can girdle sheaths and stems, kill leaves, and cause severely damaged plants to lodge.
summary.quote: The first symptom is an oblong, water-soaked lesion on leaf sheaths at or near the water line (Figure 1). In two or three days the lesion will have a grayish-white center surrounded by a dark purplish- or reddish-brown margin and may be up to one inch long.

diagnostic_features.value: Lesion with a grayish-white center surrounded by a dark purplish- or reddish-brown margin, up to one inch long, on leaf sheaths at or near the water line; white-to-brown sclerotia form on infected stem surfaces.
diagnostic_features.quote: In two or three days the lesion will have a grayish-white center surrounded by a dark purplish- or reddish-brown margin and may be up to one inch long.

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Magnaporthe oryzae (synonym Pyricularia oryzae ) is the causal agent responsible for rice blast disease.

type_of_disease.quote: Rice blast disease is one of the most devastating fungal diseases

affected_parts.quote: Rice blast can also infect various parts of a plant including leaves, sheath, neck, and panicle (Puri et al. 2009).

summary.value: Rice blast produces lesions on the leaf surface that begin as small spots and progress into diamond-shaped formations with a dark-brown color and lighter, yellowish leaf tissue around the margins; necrotic lesions can also occur on the sheath, neck, and panicle, with infected panicles turning white.
summary.quote: Most notably, rice blast disease presents distinct physical symptoms, including lesions that appear on the surface of the leaf. These lesions initially begin as small spots and progress into diamond-shaped formations, featuring a dark-brown color with lighter-colored, yellowish leaf tissue around the margins (Figure 3).

diagnostic_features.value: Leaf lesions are usually diamond shaped with a gray or white center and brown or reddish-brown border; resistant cultivars show smaller and darker lesions; diseased nodes are brown or black; neck blast causes the panicle to die prematurely, leaving it white and completely blank with unfilled kernels.
diagnostic_features.quote: Lesions that occur on the leaf are usually diamond shaped with a gray or white center and brown or reddish-brown border... Diseased nodes are brown or black... If neck blast occurs early, the entire panicle may die prematurely, leaving it white and completely blank with unfilled kernels.

conflicts.note: UC IPM lists anamorph Pyricularia oryzae and synonym Pyricularia grisea; UF/IFAS EDIS lists Pyricularia oryzae as synonym; canonical accepted name is Magnaporthe oryzae.

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Early infection of rice by brown leaf spot, Cochliobolus miyabeanus.

type_of_disease.quote: A fungus causes rice brown leaf spot disease.

affected_parts.quote: on leaves, leaf sheaths, panicles, including the glumes and seeds, of developing and mature plants ... Look for the large brown lesions, up to 2.5 cm long, on the stems under the leaf sheaths, when stripped away.

summary.value: Seedlings show small, circular, yellow-brown or brown spots girdling and distorting the leaf sheaths; later, circular to oval spots up to 10 mm long, dark brown to purple, appear on the leaves. When mature, they have light brown to grey centres surrounded by dark brown margins. On the seeds, the 'eye-spot' symptom (brown with light centres) is more pronounced.
summary.quote: Seedlings show small, circular, yellow-brown or brown spots girdling and distorting the leaf sheaths. Later, at tillering, circular to oval spots, up to 10 mm long, dark brown to purple, appear on the leaves (Photos 1&2). When mature, they have light brown to grey centres, surrounded by dark brown margins (Photos 2&3). On the seeds, the 'eye-spot' symptom (brown with light centres) is more pronounced (Photo 4).

diagnostic_features.value: Spots are similar to rice blast but appear later, are more regular in outline, and have lighter centres; black spore masses develop on the spots of both leaves and seeds.
diagnostic_features.quote: The spots are similar to rice blast (see Fact Sheet no. 242 ), but differ: i) they usually appear later, and ii) the spots are more regular in outline and have lighter centres.

look_alikes.quote: The spots are similar to rice blast (see Fact Sheet no. 242 ), but differ

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: What causes rice leaf smut is a fungus called Entyloma oryzae .

type_of_disease.quote: What causes rice leaf smut is a fungus called Entyloma oryzae .

affected_parts.quote: The characteristic sign of rice with leaf smut is the presence of small black spots on the leaves.

summary.value: Rice leaf smut appears as small black spots on the leaves; the spots are slightly raised and angular, giving the leaves the appearance of having been sprinkled with ground pepper; coverage is most complete on the oldest leaves and the tips of the most heavily infected leaves may die.
summary.quote: The characteristic sign of rice with leaf smut is the presence of small black spots on the leaves. They are slightly raised and angular and give the leaves the appearance of having been sprinkled with ground pepper. Coverage by these spots is most complete on the oldest leaves. The tips of some leaves with the most infection may die.

diagnostic_features.value: Small black spots that are slightly raised and angular, giving the leaves the appearance of having been sprinkled with ground pepper, with coverage most complete on the oldest leaves.
diagnostic_features.quote: They are slightly raised and angular and give the leaves the appearance of having been sprinkled with ground pepper. Coverage by these spots is most complete on the oldest leaves.

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Bacterial blight is caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae .

type_of_disease.quote: rice bacterial blight , deadly bacterial disease that is among the most destructive afflictions of cultivated rice

affected_parts.quote: move in the xylem, the water-conducting system of the plant ... On seedlings, leaves show grey-green streaks ... early infection may be systemic, i.e., throughout the entire plant ... Streaks also occur on the leaf sheaths and the stems of susceptible varieties.

summary.value: Bacterial blight first becomes evident as water-soaked streaks that spread from the leaf tips and margins, becoming larger and eventually releasing a milky ooze that dries into yellow droplets. Characteristic grayish white lesions then appear on the leaves, signaling the late stages of infection, when leaves dry out and die. In seedlings, the leaves dry out and wilt, a syndrome known as kresek.
summary.quote: Bacterial blight first becomes evident as water-soaked streaks that spread from the leaf tips and margins, becoming larger and eventually releasing a milky ooze that dries into yellow droplets. Characteristic grayish white lesions then appear on the leaves, signaling the late stages of infection, when leaves dry out and die. In seedlings, the leaves dry out and wilt , a syndrome known as kresek.

diagnostic_features.value: Lesions develop as water-soaked to yellow-orange stripes on leaf blades or leaf tips with a wavy margin progressing toward the leaf base; bacterial ooze resembling a milky dew drop can be observed early in the morning and later dries into small yellowish beads; wavy margins (as opposed to straight margins of Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzicola); squeezing the lower end of infected seedlings shows yellowish bacterial ooze from cut ends and plants with kresek are not easily pulled from soil.
diagnostic_features.quote: On older plants, lesions usually develop as water-soaked to yellow-orange stripes on leaf blades or leaf tips or on mechanically injured parts of leaves. Lesions have a wavy margin and progress toward the leaf base. On young lesions, bacterial ooze resembling a milky dew	nop drop can be observed early in the morning.

value: Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzicola (margins straight rather than wavy)
look_alikes.quote: Kresek on seedlings may sometimes be confused with early rice stem borer damage.

conflicts.note: Britannica uses 'Rice bacterial blight'; IRRI uses 'Bacterial blight'; Lucid uses 'Rice bacterial leaf blight'. Merged under canonical 'Bacterial Blight'.
Lucid fact sheet uses 'Rice bacterial leaf blight (also known as rice leaf blight)'.
Britannica uses full form 'pathovar'; IRRI and Lucid use abbreviated 'pv.' — these refer to the same taxon.
Britannica mentions roots: 'bacteria travel through the water from infected plants to the roots and leaves'. Lucid adds stem and vascular (xylem).

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Bacterial leaf streak is caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzicola.

type_of_disease.quote: Under humid conditions, yellow droplets of bacterial ooze, which contain masses of bacterial cells, may be observed on the surface of leaves.

affected_parts.quote: Infected plants show browning and drying of leaves.

summary.value: Symptoms initially appear as small, water-soaked, linear lesions between leaf veins. These streaks are initially dark green and later become light brown to yellowish gray. The lesions are translucent when held against the light. Entire leaves may become brown and die when the disease is very severe. Under humid conditions, yellow droplets of bacterial ooze, which contain masses of bacterial cells, may be observed on the surface of leaves.
summary.quote: Symptoms initially appear as small, water-soaked, linear lesions between leaf veins. These streaks are initially dark green and later become light brown to yellowish gray. The lesions are translucent when held against the light. Entire leaves may become brown and die when the disease is very severe. Under humid conditions, yellow droplets of bacterial ooze, which contain masses of bacterial cells, may be observed on the surface of leaves.

diagnostic_features.value: Leaf streak lesions are usually thinner than those of narrow brown spot; narrow brown spot lesions are not translucent, nor do they produce bacterial ooze. When the advancing part of the streaks are cut and placed in a glass with water, a mass of bacterial cells can usually be seen oozing out of the leaf, which makes the water turbid after five minutes. Lesion margins are straight (as opposed to wavy margins of Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae).
diagnostic_features.quote: leaf streak lesions are usually thinner than those of narrow brown spot narrow brown spot lesions are not translucent, nor do they produce bacterial ooze When the advancing part of the streaks are cut and placed in a glass with water, a mass of bacterial cells can usually be seen oozing out of the leaf, which makes the water turbid after five minutes.

look_alikes.quote: Bacterial leaf streak may be confused with narrow brown spot. ... Bacterial leaf streak may also be confused with bacterial blight.

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Comparison of bacterial panicle blight resistant (left) and susceptible (right) rice varieties inoculated with Burkholderia glumae in the field.

type_of_disease.quote: Rice leaf sheath rot symptoms caused the bacterial panicle blight pathogen.

affected_parts.quote: Bacterial panicle blight infection showing upright discolored heads and green stems. ... Rice heads with symptoms of bacterial panicle blight infection on the grain. ... Rice leaf sheath rot symptoms caused the bacterial panicle blight pathogen.

summary.value: Bacterial panicle blight produces upright discolored rice heads contrasting with healthy heads, and green stems, with a characteristic two-tone discoloration of the grain; the pathogen also causes leaf sheath rot.
summary.quote: Bacterial panicle blight infection of rice heads showing upright discolored heads compared to healthy heads. ... Bacterial panicle blight infection showing upright discolored heads and green stems. ... Bacterial panicle blight infection of rice grain showing characteristic two tone discoloration symptom.

diagnostic_features.value: Characteristic two-tone discoloration of the grain, with very early infection showing water-soaked discoloration on the lower part of the grain; upright discolored heads with green stems.
diagnostic_features.quote: Very early infection by the bacterial panicle blight pathogen of rice grain showing water soaked discoloration on the lower part of the grain.
